chunks: Al-Sadiq, peace be upon him, said:

Indeed, the souls are in the form of bodies in a tree from Paradise, asking one another and recognizing one another. When a soul arrives upon the souls, they say: Leave it, for it has escaped from a tremendous terror. Then they ask it: What did so-and-so do, and what did so-and-so do? If it says to them: I left him alive, they hope for him; and if it says to them: He has perished, they say: He has fallen, he has fallen.

key_terms.الْأَرْوَاحَ: the souls; the departed immaterial beings being described
key_terms.الْجَنَّةِ: Paradise; the blessed realm associated with these souls
key_terms.تَتَسَاءَلُ: they ask one another; mutual questioning among the souls
key_terms.تَتَعَارَفُ: they recognize one another; mutual recognition and acquaintance
key_terms.شَجَرَةٍ: a tree; the place in Paradise where the souls are described as being
key_terms.صِفَةِ الْأَجْسَادِ: the form of bodies; a bodily likeness or recognizable form
key_terms.هَوَى: he has fallen; an expression of loss or ruin
key_terms.هَوْلٍ عَظِيمٍ: a tremendous terror; the grave ordeal from which the arriving soul escaped

ai.seo_question: What does Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام say about the souls after death and their condition in Paradise?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the state of souls in the hereafter, portraying them as remaining aware, mutually recognizing one another, and inquiring about those still in worldly life. It indicates an intermediate post-death condition connected to Paradise and reflects both the terror of death and the continuing concern of souls for others.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.593 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:

"The souls are in the form of bodies in a tree of Paradise; they converse and recognize one another. When a soul joins them, they say, 'Leave it, for it has escaped a great terror.'
Then they ask it, 'What did such-and-such person do, and what did such-and-such person do?'
If it responds, 'I left them alive,' they have hope for them.
But if it responds, 'They have died,' they say, 'They have fallen.'".
